questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Why a nucleus weighs less than the sum of its parts
questions.learningObjective: Explain mass defect physically
questions.stem: Explain why a bound nucleus weighs less than its separate nucleons.

answer.exemplar: When nucleons bind, energy is released. By E=mc^2 this released binding energy corresponds to a loss of mass, so the nucleus is lighter than its parts.

questions.explanation: Binding releases energy, which by mass-energy equivalence reduces mass. The difference is the mass defect.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Mass defect of iron-56 expressed in kilograms
questions.learningObjective: Compute energy from mass defect kg
questions.stem: Mass defect 8.77e-28 kg; binding energy in J? (c = 3e8)
questions.explanation: E = mc^2 = 8.77e-28 times 9e16 = 7.89e-11 J. Using c not squared gives 2.63e-19 J, wrong.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Why a nucleus weighs less than the sum of its parts
questions.learningObjective: Identify the force responsible
questions.stem: The mass defect arises from the

options.misconception: weak force causes decay, not binding

questions.explanation: The strong nuclear force binds nucleons, releasing binding energy and causing mass defect. Electromagnetic, gravitational, and weak forces are not responsible.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Binding energy per nucleon of uranium-238
questions.learningObjective: Compute mass defect of U-238 from BE
questions.stem: Uranium-238 total BE 1802 MeV; mass defect in u? (1 u = 931.5 MeV)
questions.explanation: 1802 divided by 931.5 = 1.934 u. Multiplying gives 1.68e6, too large.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: How much tighter iron-56 is bound than uranium-238 per nucleon
questions.learningObjective: Explain energy release in fusion and fission
questions.stem: Explain why both fission of heavy nuclei and fusion of light nuclei release energy.

answer.exemplar: Both processes move nuclei toward the peak of the binding energy curve near iron. Increasing BE per nucleon releases energy in either direction.

questions.explanation: Fission of heavy nuclei and fusion of light nuclei both increase BE per nucleon toward the iron peak, releasing energy.
